title: Every class with code reaches the diagnostic mixin
owner: cairn (cairn/machines/build_inspector is the sieve's address; CC builds)
intention: Every class in cairn/ whose body holds code inherits DiagnosticBase, so when we get stuck any of them can produce a diagnostic report for the inspector to read. A build_inspector sieve reds a class that does not.
why: Akien 2026-10-27: 'everybody must inherit it. that's why it's a mixin' / 'any class with code it in should be able to run a diagnostic report when we need it.' The origin is his test framework, made into an inspectable state machine. A stack trace says where something failed but not the selector, the timeout, the data values or a hidden retry, so re-running tests just to get more data is the waste he removed. For that, diagnostics must sit in the lowest class everything inherits from. Today only devices and shims get it by construction. A census on 2026-10-27 found 94 classes with a method body in cairn/; 31 reach the mixin and 63 do not.
traces_to: Law 1 (a failure whose data is already in the log is never re-run); Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces); Law 4 (the rule becomes a sieve, not prose); concept-piece CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass.md
how: One new sieve, every_class_reaches_the_diagnostic_mixin, in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py, registered in SIEVES, plus one proof file. The conversions of the 63 standing classes are per-component sibling tickets, cast after this one, with this sieve's red list as their queue (the 56d1aff4455e precedent). See the decisions D1-D7.
falsifier: RED if any of the following holds: the sieve passes a class whose own body defines a function and that has no route to DiagnosticBase; it reds a class that reaches the mixin directly or through a same-repo base; it reds a method-less class; it reds the Probe root, or passes a Probe subclass with a method that does not reach the mixin; it passes a base expression it could not resolve; it judges a file under proofs/; live, on cairn/, its findings differ from the census set with no named reason; or any existing build_inspector proof goes red. Wrong intent if Akien's 'class with code' means something narrower than a class whose body defines a function.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [FIXME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> PROVED
watchme: none, because the sieve is its own watch: every inspection re-runs it and its findings fold into one standing trouble per sieve (cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py _finding_trouble_id), read at every session open. The list draining to zero is visible there with no probe. Whether the intention worked is answered by the sibling conversion tickets reaching PROVED.

decisions.text: D1: PLACE AND NAME. The sieve is a function every_class_reaches_the_diagnostic_mixin(row, comp_dir) -> list[dict] in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py, added to the SIEVES dict beside encapsulation_holds and built from _finding(...) like its neighbours. Its docstring carries the provenance: Akien's words from open-4141d959b634, open-d32047bb1759 and open-d7983cf68dd2, and this ticket id.

D2: THE PREDICATE. Walk every .py file under comp_dir that address.component_of attributes to this row (deepest owner), excluding any path with a proofs/ segment and __pycache__. For every ast.ClassDef at any depth whose own body directly contains an ast.FunctionDef or ast.AsyncFunctionDef (properties and staticmethods count; inherited or generated methods do not), the class must REACH DiagnosticBase, else it is one finding. A class with no def in its own body is never judged.

D3: REACH. A class reaches DiagnosticBase if any base expression resolves to the class cairn.tools.base.diagnostic.DiagnosticBase, or to a repo class that itself reaches it, checked recursively with cycle protection. Resolution reads the module's own ast imports: 'from X import Y [as Z]' and 'import X [as Z]' with an attribute chain, plus classes defined in the same module. A base that resolves to a module outside the repo (stdlib or third-party: Exception, ABC, ModuleType, dict, a call like type(Path())) is non-reaching, and the class is judged by its other bases. A base whose name resolves to nothing (not defined, not imported, a star import) is a finding of its own with reason 'unresolvable base', never a pass (Law 7). A dotted-module name that cannot be found on disk under the repo also counts as outside the repo.

decisions.by: Akien (open-d7983cf68dd2) for member (b); cc for (a) and (c)
decisions.text: D4: EXEMPTIONS ARE A RULE OF THREE MEMBERS, never a list of names that grows. (a) DiagnosticBase itself, because the mixin cannot inherit itself. (b) The Probe ROOT class, cairn/tools/base/probe.py::Probe, matched by module and name. Akien: 'determination isn't made at the rootmost level, but as each subclass needs.' A subclass of Probe with a def in its body is judged like any other class. (c) Any file under a proofs/ directory: fixture classes there measure the system rather than run in it, following the address_rule precedent (cairn/tools/base/address_rule.py). This member is CC's call; if Akien wants proof fixtures covered, it is one line.

D5: FINDINGS. One finding per class: _finding('every_class_reaches_the_diagnostic_mixin', row['component'], '<file>:<line> class <Name> has code and does not reach DiagnosticBase', expected=True, actual=False, file=<repo-relative path>, line=<lineno>, cls=<Name>, reason='no route' | 'unresolvable base: <expr>'). It uses the existing one-trouble-per-sieve fold unchanged. A component with no readable .py yields []: such a component has no classes to judge, unlike address_rule, where reading zero files is a hollow scan.

D6: THE PROOF. Create cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_every_class_reaches_the_diagnostic_mixin.py, runnable bare with python3 (exit 0 = green), each tooth building its own temp component tree with tempfile and calling the sieve through cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector at call time, never at import. Teeth: (1) a class with a def and no bases is red; (2) 'from cairn.tools.base.diagnostic import DiagnosticBase' plus 'class A(DiagnosticBase)' with a def is green; (3) class B(A) in another module of the fixture, importing A, is green through the chain; (4) a class with only a docstring and attributes is not judged; (5) a fixture cairn/tools/base/probe.py::Probe with defs is not judged, and class P2(Probe) with a def and no mixin is red; (6) class C(Missing) with a def, where Missing is not defined or imported, is red with reason starting 'unresolvable base'; (7) a red class in <comp>/proofs/x.py is not judged; (8) class E(Exception) with a def is red, and class F(DiagnosticBase, Exception) with a def is green; (9) live: the sieve's findings over the real cairn/ census rows equal the set an independent ast census gives, each finding naming file:line, as invariants, never a pinned count; (10) the sieve is registered: 'every_class_reaches_the_diagnostic_mixin' in inspector.SIEVES. The fixture tree mirrors the repo layout (<tmp>/cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py defining DiagnosticBase), so resolution is tested, not assumed.

D7: OUT OF SCOPE. Editing any class in any other component to add the mixin (those are sibling tickets); module-level functions (Akien ruled classes); skills/, bin/ and launchers/ (the census root is cairn/, the same as device_census); and narrowing diagnostic_inspector's falsifier (5), which happens in its sibling ticket. Runtime issubclass checks by importing modules are also out: the sieve is a deterministic AST read and imports nothing it judges.

D8: FIXTURE REPAIR. test_inspector.py's fixture components say 'from base import BaseDevice' and define class D(BaseDevice) with a def, so the new sieve would red its healthy component and break tooth 1. main() writes <tmp>/base.py (beside the census root tmp/cairn, outside it) holding 'from cairn.tools.base.diagnostic import DiagnosticBase' and 'class BaseDevice(DiagnosticBase): pass', so the sieve resolves module 'base' to <repo_root>/base.py and D reaches the mixin. Tooth 1b asserts the sieve is in SIEVES, yields [] on healthy, and yields exactly [(D, line 4, 'no route')] when base.py loses the mixin (restored after). Its PROVES entry is 339a45cee6a1 'all', and test_inspector.py joins proven_by. Already committed red-first at 618fd6f8.
decisions.step: give test_inspector's fixture a route to DiagnosticBase

decisions.text: D8 (above) settles this step: the fixture's base module reaches DiagnosticBase, and tooth 1b proves it.
decisions.step: Modify cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py fixture to prevent it from reding when the new sieve runs

decisions.text: D10: WHERE THE FIXTURE REPAIR LIVES. It is a change to test_inspector.py's main() only, not to _component() and not to the new proof. main() writes <tmp>/base.py once, before the first _component call. The new proof does not need it: its fixtures import DiagnosticBase from <tmp>/cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py directly. Both files are already edited and committed (618fd6f8); the build edits only inspector.py.

D3 ALGORITHM (as built at 7dfc3990): a _Modules cache parses each repo module once and holds its ast imports ('from X import Y [as Z]', 'import X [as Z]') and its ClassDefs as a name table; _reach_expr resolves a base Name or Attribute through that table, _reach_symbol follows 'from src import name' to a class in src or a submodule of it, and _reach_class recurses through the resolved class's bases with a seen-set against cycles; a module is in the repo when its dotted path maps to a .py file or package under the repo root, otherwise it is outside and non-reaching
